title: Chain complexes of modules and their homology
statement: Let $R$ be a ring. A *chain complex* $C_\bullet$ of $R$-modules consists of $R$-modules $C_n$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, and $R$-linear maps $d_n:C_n\to C_{n-1}$ (the differentials) with $d_{n-1}\circ d_n=0$ for all $n$; a complex given only in degrees $n\ge0$ (or in a finite range) is extended by $C_n=0$ and $d_n=0$ in the other degrees. A *morphism* $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ of chain complexes is a family of $R$-linear maps $f_n:C_n\to D_n$ with $d^D_n\circ f_n=f_{n-1}\circ d^C_n$. Since $d_n\circ d_{n+1}=0$, $\operatorname{im}d_{n+1}\subseteq\ker d_n$, and the *$n$-th homology module* of $C_\bullet$ is the $R$-module $$H_n(C_\bullet)=\ker(d_n:C_n\to C_{n-1})/\operatorname{im}(d_{n+1}:C_{n+1}\to C_n).$$ A morphism $f$ maps $\ker d^C_n$ into $\ker d^D_n$ and $\operatorname{im}d^C_{n+1}$ into $\operatorname{im}d^D_{n+1}$ and so induces an $R$-linear map $H_n(f):H_n(C_\bullet)\to H_n(D_\bullet)$, compatible with composition and identities.
